title_en: TTU153: Why Investors Keep Getting Trend Following Wrong ft. Patrick Welton
title_zh: TTU153：为什么投资者总是误解趋势跟踪 ft. Patrick Welton（Welton Investment Corporation）
subtitle_zh: Patrick Welton 谈趋势跟踪的道德义务、四个S框架、复制、容量与市场状态。
description: TTU153: Why Investors Keep Getting Trend Following Wrong ft. Patrick Welton

turns.en: It's the usual tragedy of managed money to watch people watch performance, wait for there to be enough confirmation and confidence, get in a little bit too late and put themselves on a right shift of time off cycle.
turns.zh: 这就是受托资金管理（managed money）常见的悲剧：眼睁睁看着大家盯着业绩，等到有足够的确认和信心才进场，结果进得稍微晚了点，把自己放到了一个错开周期的时间右移上。

turns.en: Welcome to Top Traders Unplugged. In markets, success doesn't come from predicting what happens next. It comes from being prepared for what you can't predict.
turns.zh: 欢迎收听 Top Traders Unplugged。在市场里，成功并不来自预测接下来会发生什么，而是来自为你无法预测的事情做好准备。

turns.en: In each episode, we go deep with some of the world's most thoughtful minds in investing, economics and beyond to understand how they think, how they prepare and how they decide, and the experiences that shaped how they see the world.
turns.zh: 在每一期节目里，我们都会与全球投资、经济及相关领域中最善于思考的一些头脑深入交流，去理解他们如何思考、如何准备、如何决策，以及那些塑造了他们看待世界方式的经历。

turns.en: No noise, no shortcuts, just real conversations to help you think better and invest with confidence.
turns.zh: 没有噪音，没有捷径，只有真实的对话，帮助你更好地思考、更有信心地投资。

turns.en: Hey, everyone, and welcome to another edition of Top Traders Unplugged, where today Alan Dunn and I are delighted to be joined by Pat Weldon and founder and CEO of Welton Investment Corporation as part of our series focusing on the one investment strategy that we have dedicated pretty much all of our careers to, namely trend following and managed futures more broadly.
turns.zh: 嘿，大家好，欢迎收听新一期的 Top Traders Unplugged。今天 Alan Dunne 和我非常高兴请到了 Pat Welton，他是 Welton Investment Corporation 的创始人兼 CEO。这是我们那个系列的一部分，聚焦于我们几乎把整个职业生涯都投入其中的那一种投资策略，也就是趋势跟踪（trend following），以及更广义的 managed futures。

turns.en: First off, Pat, it's really great to have you on the podcast. Thanks so much for joining us today. We really have been looking forward to our conversation. I hope you're doing well.
turns.zh: 首先，Pat，真的很高兴你能来上我们的播客。非常感谢你今天加入我们。我们真的很期待这次对话。希望你一切都好。

turns.en: I am doing well and thanks for inviting me. Absolutely. I'm actually, maybe more importantly, as I told you the other day, thank you for all you do for the trading community.
turns.zh: 我很好，谢谢你们的邀请，真的很感谢。其实，也许更重要的是，就像我前几天跟你们说的，感谢你们为交易圈所做的一切。

turns.en: You've probably built the single largest and best resource to help traders and investors that they could find anywhere.
turns.zh: 你们可能打造出了交易者和投资者在任何地方都能找到的最庞大、最好的资源。

turns.en: That's very kind of you to say. Thank you so much. And of course, we do it because we have contributors like yourself, so that's how we can do it. Alan, it's also great to see you. How are you doing? How is Dublin treating you?
turns.zh: 你这么说真是太客气了，非常感谢。当然，我们之所以能做这些，是因为有像你这样的贡献者，所以我们才做得成。Alan，也很高兴见到你。你最近怎么样？Dublin 待得还舒服吗？

turns.en: Dublin? Very good, yeah. Great to be on and looking forward to speaking with yourself and Pat. I'm sure we'll have a lot to delve into.
turns.zh: Dublin 吗？非常好，是的。很高兴能来上节目，期待和你还有 Pat 一起聊。我相信我们会有很多可以深入探讨的东西。

turns.en: Yes, absolutely. Now, before we get into all of the different topics we're going to be discussing, I would like to set the stage a little bit for our conversation so that the audience knows a little bit about your background.
turns.zh: 是的，当然。在我们进入要讨论的各个不同话题之前，我想先为我们这次对话铺垫一下，好让听众对你的背景有些了解。

turns.en: Pat. But instead of doing the usual list of places you worked and all of that stuff, I was hoping that maybe you could tell us about maybe 2, 3 pivotal points in your career where you experienced something profound that shaped how you think about investing and maybe also kind of led to where you are specifically today.
turns.zh: Pat。不过，与其按老套路列一遍你工作过的地方之类的，我更希望你能跟我们讲讲你职业生涯中两三个关键的转折点——那些你经历了某些深刻的事情、塑造了你对投资的思考、也许还直接造就了你今天所处位置的时刻。

turns.en: Wow. Well, you know, when you're 65 years old, there's definitely been a few pivots, especially in this industry.
turns.zh: 哇。嗯，你知道，当你到了 65 岁，肯定经历过好几次转折，尤其是在这个行业里。

turns.en: Tell me about it. You Know, I think for those who know me and know that I'm a physician and know that I started a hedge fund years ago and the, the usual three pivots that I get asked about are something like why medicine, why trading?
turns.zh: 可不是嘛。你知道，我想对于那些了解我、知道我是医生、也知道我多年前创办了一只对冲基金的人来说，人们常问我的那三个转折大致是：为什么选医学，为什么做交易？

turns.en: And. And then when they hear those, then the most perplexing one is they say why both.
turns.zh: 然后，等他们听完这两个，最令人费解的那个问题就是：为什么两个都做。

turns.en: So the we could delve into those. Why medicine's a pretty short story and mostly about working in a cancer laboratory and why trading really is a, a life pivot. Because that really is also how fortunate I was to meet my wife and co founder Annette.
turns.zh: 所以这些我们都可以深入聊聊。为什么选医学，这是个很短的故事，主要就是在一个癌症实验室工作的经历；而为什么做交易，那真是一次人生转折，因为也正是通过它，我才如此幸运地遇到了我的妻子、也是联合创始人的 Annette。

turns.en: And why both is. It's a, it's a multi legged story but the capstone of it was probably a very kind Paul Tudor Jones that Annette and I went to visit many, many, many years ago that gave us some resolve afterwards.
turns.zh: 至于为什么两个都做，那是个有很多条线索的故事，但它的顶点，大概是很多很多很多年前 Annette 和我去拜访的那位非常和善的 Paul Tudor Jones，那次见面之后给了我们一些决心。

turns.en: So like to delve into any of those? Yeah, actually, you know, because you have a very interesting background and obviously it dates back to the commodities Corp. Days and many people don't really know how important I think that that company was.
turns.zh: 那想深入聊聊其中哪些吗？好啊，其实你知道，因为你的背景非常有意思，而且显然可以追溯到 Commodities Corporation 的年代，很多人并不真正了解我认为那家公司曾经有多重要。

turns.en: Not that I want to spend too much time on it, but I mean of course it could be fun and interesting maybe just to hear one or two short stories.
turns.zh: 倒不是我想在这上面花太多时间，但我的意思是，听一两个小故事当然会挺有趣、挺有意思的。

turns.en: You had mentors. You mentioned Paul Tudor Jones. I think you know, John Henry. There are others that are well, very well known people from our industry.
turns.zh: 你有过一些导师。你提到了 Paul Tudor Jones，我想还有 John Henry，还有其他一些在我们这个行业里非常知名的人。

turns.en: If you have a few things you can share that would of course make it very, very interesting. That will probably help condense 40 years into a smaller number. But so sort of spinning my way up.
turns.zh: 如果你有几件事可以分享，那当然会非常非常有意思，大概也能帮我们把 40 年浓缩成更短的篇幅。那我就顺着往上讲讲我的经历吧。

turns.en: I ended up changing initials college studies into medicine, received a grant for a medical scientist training program which led me to ucla, which is also where I met Annette, the very first person I met at ucla.
turns.zh: 我最后把大学一开始的专业转向了医学，拿到了一份 medical scientist training program（医学科学家培训项目）的资助，这把我带到了 UCLA，也正是那里我遇到了 Annette——她是我在 UCLA 遇到的第一个人。

turns.en: So I've warned young people for years, be very careful who you get into an elevator with.
turns.zh: 所以我多年来一直提醒年轻人：跟你一起进电梯的人是谁，一定要非常小心。

turns.en: You might be there for a long time. And that subsequently led to really I think to some degree US trading personally to make some ends meet. But with Annette's entrepreneurialism and sort of striving, we ended up getting discovered, if you will, when we were up in the Palo Alto area when we since moved to Stanford and one thing led to another and we were introduced to commodities corporations.
turns.zh: 你可能会在里面待很久。后来这也在一定程度上促使我们俩自己去做交易，赚点钱贴补生活。但凭着 Annette 的创业精神和那股拼劲，我们最终算是被“发掘”了——当时我们在 Palo Alto 一带，后来又搬到了 Stanford，一件事接一件事，我们被引荐给了 Commodities Corporation。

turns.en: So we learned about them much like somebody today might. If you roll back into the late 1980s commodities corporation I think could, could reasonably be thought of as the very first multi strategy pod shop of traders.
turns.zh: 所以我们对他们的了解，就跟今天的人去了解一家机构差不多。如果把时间倒回到 1980 年代末，我认为 Commodities Corporation 完全可以被看作是第一家多策略（multi-strategy）的“pod shop”交易商。

turns.en: I think of them as much more dimensional than that though because they also were very explicitly in the business of developing trading talent.
turns.zh: 不过在我看来，他们的内涵远比这更丰富，因为他们还非常明确地在做培养交易人才这件事。

turns.en: They had senior traders, they had that Oftentimes mentored juniors. They had facilities that, you know, helped junior traders work. And one thing led to another and we were offered a contract to trade for them.
turns.zh: 他们有资深交易员，这些资深交易员经常指导新人；他们还有各种设施，帮助初级交易员开展工作。然后一件事接一件事，我们收到了一份为他们做交易的合约。

turns.en: So while we were trading for ourselves initially and thinking we might be saving up some money for some kind of opportunity to explore later in life, it turned out the trading itself became the opportunity when we turned professional and started trading for them.
turns.zh: 所以一开始我们只是为自己做交易，想着也许能攒点钱，等以后有机会再去探索别的事情；结果当我们转为职业、开始为他们做交易时，交易本身反倒成了那个机会。

turns.en: And that really sort of leads to the mentorship that we learned from many other traders. And there are many others that we met. And we learned a lot from some of the very biggest names in the industry that you and I might know, some of which aren't even in the industry today.
turns.zh: 而这也真正引出了我们从许多其他交易员那里得到的指导。我们还遇到过很多其他人，从行业里一些你我可能都知道的最响亮的名字身上学到了很多，其中有些人如今甚至已经不在这一行了。

turns.en: For instance, like John Henry. True. But there was one episode.
turns.zh: 比如说 John Henry，确实如此。不过其中有那么一段经历。

turns.en: We were still thinking about medicine as a primary career, and trading was just on the side.
turns.zh: 那时我们还在把医学当作主要的职业方向，交易只是副业。

turns.en: It was just simply a profession for us. And we hadn't really thought about developing a separate company. But I do remember when we in 89, we had sort of had a really good start with cc.
turns.zh: 对我们来说它只是一份职业而已，我们还没真正想过要成立一家独立的公司。但我确实记得，在 89 年，我们在 CC（Commodities Corporation）那边有了一个非常好的开局。

turns.en: We were allocated more money every quarter. As we hit return targets.
turns.zh: 每当达到回报目标，我们每个季度都会被分配更多的资金。

turns.en: By 1990 or so, we, you know, were trading sort of more and more money and met more traders along the way.
turns.zh: 到 1990 年前后，我们交易的资金越来越多，一路上也结识了更多交易员。

turns.en: And it was about that time that Elaine Crocker, who was the head of Commodities Corp's trading at the time, called ahead for us and said we should really meet Paul Tudor Jones. And so she brokered that.
turns.zh: 大约就在那时候，当时担任 Commodities Corporation 交易主管的 Elaine Crocker 替我们提前打了招呼，说我们真应该去见见 Paul Tudor Jones。于是她促成了这次见面。

turns.en: And though it was long ago, Paul was already very famous as a trader. Even that many years ago, he is just a standout natural talent.
turns.zh: 尽管那是很久以前的事了，Paul 作为交易员当时就已经非常有名。哪怕在那么多年前，他也已经是一位极其出众的天才。

turns.en: So we really looked forward to meeting him. And I still remember that day because we arrived and one of his colleagues, I think his name was Sean, met us and he guided us in and showed us about the office.
turns.zh: 所以我们真的很期待见到他。我至今还记得那一天，因为我们到的时候，他的一位同事——我记得他叫 Sean——接待了我们，带我们进去，还带我们参观了办公室。

turns.en: We waited for a little while and sort of in the distance we could see, at one point we could see Paul very sort of engaged, intensely engaged on a phone screen, you know, looking at something walking about.
turns.zh: 我们等了一会儿，隔着一定距离，有那么一刻我们能看到 Paul 非常投入、全神贯注地盯着一个电话屏幕，一边看着什么一边来回走动。

turns.en: And we were delayed and delayed and delayed. And we were thinking we might be meeting him for a five minute handshake or something. But after about 15 minutes, just this remarkable thing happened. He sort of came out of his office, all intensity was gone.
turns.zh: 我们被一拖再拖再拖。当时我们想，也许最后就是跟他握个手、见个五分钟之类的。但大约 15 分钟后，一件很了不起的事情发生了：他走出办公室，那股紧绷的专注劲儿全没了。

turns.en: He was fully gracious and welcoming and kind and, you know, apologizing us to us as sort of trading nobodies from Commodities Corporation for his being late.
turns.zh: 他完全是一副亲切、热情、和善的样子，还向我们这两个来自 Commodities Corporation 的交易界无名小卒道歉，因为他迟到了。

turns.en: And then almost instantaneously, he offered us one of, I think, the greatest trading lessons we ever learned.
turns.zh: 然后几乎是一瞬间，他就给了我们一个我认为是我们这辈子学过的最伟大的交易课之一。

turns.en: He said in this sort of marvelous Southern Memphis accent that he had at the time, which was much stronger then than I'VE heard him recently on interviews, but I still remember him saying no. He says, Pat Nanette, he starts going on one thing is that when you start trading size, you can't only think about getting out when you want.
turns.zh: 他用当时那种很棒的南方 Memphis 口音说话，那口音比我现在在采访里听到的要重得多。我至今还记得他说的话。他说：“Pat、Annette，”他接着讲，“有一点是，当你开始交易很大的量（size）时，你不能只想着在你想出场的时候出场。”

turns.en: You have to get out when the market lets you. And from there forward, I could never sort of unsee the obvious, that markets weren't math, that there's somebody on the other side of every single trade who at that moment believes they also have an edge.
turns.zh: “你得在市场让你出场的时候出场。”从那以后，我再也没法对这个显而易见的事实视而不见了：市场不是数学，每一笔交易的对家都有一个人，在那一刻相信自己同样拥有优势（edge）。

turns.en: And I'm sure as we wander on other topics, that theme is going to come up again and again.
turns.zh: 我确信，随着我们聊到其他话题，这个主题还会一次又一次地出现。

turns.en: Market structure matters. The second thing we did was we walked around his office, had this marvelous tour, his graciousness, humor, all everywhere,
turns.zh: 市场结构（market structure）很重要。我们做的第二件事是在他办公室里走了走，进行了一次很棒的参观，他的亲切和幽默无处不在，

turns.en: telling us one short story after another. And he's pointing out the desks and pointing out the facilities. And then he said something like.
turns.zh: 一个接一个地给我们讲小故事。他一边指着那些桌子、指着那些设施，然后他说了类似这样的话——

turns.en: Which just from memory was something like, when you grow, you need more things, you need more people, you need more capital.
turns.zh: 凭记忆大致是：当你规模变大，你就需要更多东西，你需要更多人，需要更多资本。

turns.en: He said, and then it starts getting funny. And so now we have manuals for this, we have manuals for that, and now we have manuals for all the manuals.
turns.zh: 他说，然后就变得好笑了：于是现在我们有这本手册、那本手册，现在我们还为所有这些手册准备了手册。

turns.en: And of course, we're all laughing at this point. But we left that meeting and the lesson was really clear for us, was that trading was only one. One component of building a professional trading firm.
turns.zh: 当然，这时候我们全都笑了。但我们离开那次会议时，得到的教训非常清楚：交易只是建立一家专业交易公司的其中一个组成部分。

turns.en: And we digested those lessons for years. And ultimately that's after sort of processing them. We decided that if we built a small firm, even if one that was a tenth or the twentieth the size of Tudor, that we might be able to fully separate the missions of medicine, whether they were practicing or teaching or research or any combination from money.
turns.zh: 我们花了好几年去消化这些教训。最终，在把它们想明白之后，我们决定：如果我们建立一家小公司，哪怕规模只有 Tudor 的十分之一或二十分之一，我们也许就能把医学的使命——无论是行医、教学、研究，还是几者的任意组合——与赚钱彻底分开。

turns.en: You know, we could solve for them separately. And so afterwards, we decided to build a small firm and we began taking in outside money. And that's what Welton is today. And even in retrospect, it seems naive, but it's exactly what became true.
turns.zh: 你知道，我们可以分别去解决这两件事。所以后来，我们决定建一家小公司，并开始引入外部资金。这就是 Welton 今天的由来。即便回头去看这显得有些天真，但它恰恰成了现实。

turns.en: And it's been a guiding principle for us since the start. Yeah, wonderful, wonderful story. Thank you so much for sharing that.
turns.zh: 从一开始，这就是我们的一条指导原则。是啊，真是精彩、精彩的故事。非常感谢你分享这些。

turns.en: I have to say, I think these stories from around the time when I began as well, I think they're so important. And there are some people in this industry that have, yeah, really got some amazing lessons that they have shared along the way.
turns.zh: 我得说，这些故事差不多也发生在我刚入行的那段时间，我觉得它们太重要了。这个行业里有些人，是的，真的获得了一些很了不起的教训，并且一路分享了出来。

turns.en: So I appreciate that. Now, Alan and I, and you, we spoke a few days ago because you brought along a lot of great ideas in terms of what we could be talking about.
turns.zh: 所以我很感激这一点。是这样的，几天前 Alan、我和你聊过一次，因为你带来了很多关于我们能聊些什么的好点子。

turns.en: And what we have done since then is we've kind of tried to divide topics up into the usual headlines, if you like. That we normally talk about when we do this particular series.
turns.zh: 从那之后我们做的，就是试着把话题分成那些惯常的大标题，如果你愿意这么说的话——也就是我们做这个特定系列时通常会谈到的那些。

turns.en: And so what I will do in, in the usual tradition is I'm going to kick it over to you, Alan, to, to start off.
turns.zh: 所以按照老规矩，我要把话头交给你，Alan，由你来开场。

turns.en: Great. Well, maybe to pick up on that. And I suppose evolution that you talked about, Pat, in terms of medicine to trading. And then I suppose what came next was an asset management business. And obviously it was one of the themes you kind of touched on in your own notes, the transition from being a prop trader to running an asset management business, which you've mentioned again there.
turns.zh: 好的。那也许就顺着这个来讲。我想，Pat，你谈到的从医学到交易的这种演变，接下来大概就是资产管理业务了。这显然也是你在自己那份笔记里提到过的主题之一——从一名自营交易员（prop trader）转变为经营一家资产管理业务，你刚才又提到了这点。

turns.en: So just curious, maybe if you could delve into that a bit more. Obviously, when you run an asset management business, there's the old business side that comes with that in terms of compliance and sales, business development, et cetera.
turns.zh: 所以挺好奇的，也许你可以再深入讲讲。显然，当你经营一家资产管理业务时，随之而来的是那些老套的商业事务，比如合规、销售、业务拓展等等。

turns.en: But I'm more interested in kind of the risk management and the trading.
turns.zh: 但我更感兴趣的是风险管理和交易这一块。

turns.en: Does that differ when you're just trading as a prop trader for yourself, but purely just yourself accountable to then thinking about, okay, we're going to get into the business of managing risk and generating returns for outside investors and how that evolved and how you've thought about that over the years.
turns.zh: 当你只是作为自营交易员为自己做交易、纯粹只对自己负责，到后来开始考虑“好，我们要进入为外部投资者管理风险、创造回报的生意”时，这中间有区别吗？这种转变是如何演化的，这些年来你又是怎么思考的？

turns.en: You know, I think that's a question that doesn't receive enough attention.
turns.zh: 你知道，我觉得这是个没有得到足够重视的问题。

turns.en: And we sort of. Or if it does receive attention, it's the mechanisms of building the firm kind of the lessons we introduced, the compliance, the operations, the regulations, et cetera.
turns.zh: 我们多少……或者说，如果它真的受到了关注，那关注的也是建立公司的种种机制，也就是我们前面提到的那些教训：合规、运营、监管等等。

turns.en: That's not really the big difference. I think the real big difference is a moral difference.
turns.zh: 但那其实并不是最大的区别。我认为真正的大区别是一种道德上的区别。

turns.en: When you're a proprietary trader and to make it easy for yourself,
turns.zh: 当你是一名自营交易员时，为了让自己省事，

turns.en: you would have one set of goals and hopefully they've been sharply defined because if they're not, that's going to be a principal weakness. And we could talk about that separately.
turns.zh: 你会有一套目标，而且希望这套目标被清晰地界定过，因为如果没有，那就会成为一个主要的弱点。这一点我们可以另外单独聊。

turns.en: But I think the minute you take in outside money, you really take in the moral obligation that it's their goals that are most important for what you do with that money, which shapes everything.
turns.zh: 但我认为，从你引入外部资金的那一刻起，你就真正承担了一种道德义务：用这笔钱去做什么，最重要的是他们的目标，而这会塑造一切。

turns.en: It shapes the very heart of the question you just asked. How is risk managed in their particular world? If they're more like an allocator than an investor, they might want something that is more consistently exposed and more constant and targeted volatility, as it would be known today.
turns.zh: 它塑造了你刚才那个问题的核心：在他们那个特定的世界里，风险是如何管理的？如果他们更像是配置者（allocator）而不是投资者，他们可能会想要一个敞口更持续、更恒定、带有目标波动率（targeted volatility）——用今天的说法——的东西。

turns.en: If they were more of an investor, they might want more exposure when there's a better value or when there's a better forward return profile and less exposure when it's weaker, because there is a sense of wanting to have your investment size proportionate to return.
turns.zh: 如果他们更像是投资者，他们可能会在价值更好、或者未来回报前景更好的时候想要更多敞口，在其变弱时想要更少敞口，因为有一种想法是希望自己的投资规模与回报成正比。

turns.en: But I think it all stems from really that moral difference that the day you take somebody's Outside money is the day you make their goals. The number one goal.
turns.zh: 但我认为这一切都源于那种道德上的区别：你收下别人外部资金的那一天，就是你把他们的目标当作头号目标的那一天。

turns.en: If you were turning it into any kind of a formula, the formula is probably different because most prop traders for themselves are probably thinking something on the order of a ray rock, right? A risk adjusted rate of return on capital.
turns.zh: 如果你要把它变成某种公式，那公式很可能是不一样的，因为大多数为自己做交易的自营交易员，想的大概是类似 RAROC 这样的东西，对吧？也就是经风险调整后的资本回报率（risk-adjusted rate of return on capital）。

turns.en: So they think in dollars more than they think in percents. I mean with that in mind then obviously does that presumably it informs you of the kinds of programs you offer and the blends and the levels of volatility and, and, and everything that that that goes with that.
turns.zh: 所以他们更多的是以美元金额、而不是以百分比来思考。我的意思是，考虑到这一点，那显然——大概——这会影响你们提供哪些类型的程序、它们的组合搭配、波动率水平，以及与之相关的一切吧？

turns.en: Presumably absolutely. And, and, and it has over the years. You know, when we first began trading outside money we, we traded a what would be classified today as more or less a diversified
turns.zh: 大概是的，绝对会。而且这些年来确实如此。你知道，当我们刚开始交易外部资金时，我们交易的是一个用今天的标准来分类、多少算是一个多元化的

turns.en: medium term trend following program with a few shorter term elements. In it.
turns.zh: 中期趋势跟踪程序，里面还带有一些更短周期的元素。

turns.en: That was not traded at a fixed volatility. The volatility would ebb and flow within a range though its average volatility would be in, in Approximately probably about a 15 volume in the 90s, but that might be 10 volume when there's less opportunity and 20 when there's more something, something like that amplitude range.
turns.zh: 它并不是以一个固定的波动率来交易的。波动率会在一个区间内起伏，不过它的平均波动率大概——在 90 年代大约是 15 的波动率（vol），机会少的时候可能是 10，机会多的时候是 20，大致是这么一个幅度区间。

turns.en: Later on in the early 2000s there were I still remember actually of a very pivotal meeting. I was speaking for one of the French bank circuits that were popular at the time. And after my speech we were gathered in one of the restaurants
turns.zh: 后来在 2000 年代初，我其实还记得一次非常关键的会面。当时我在为一家法国银行的巡回路演做演讲，那在当时很流行。演讲结束后，我们聚集在

turns.en: in the hotel outside of Florence and three pretty well known people in the industry, maybe even people who've been on the podcast. At one point in time I remember us all being at the table and them asking a really serious question.
turns.zh: Florence 郊外一家酒店的餐厅里，还有三位在业内相当知名的人，也许甚至是上过这档播客的人。我记得有那么一刻我们大家围坐在桌边，他们问了一个非常严肃的问题。

turns.en: There's like why? Why when I have an account with some professional traders do I seem to lose money three or four times faster than I make money?
turns.zh: 问题大致是：为什么？为什么当我在某个专业交易员那里开了账户时，我亏钱的速度好像比赚钱快三四倍？

turns.en: And I of course thought it was an observation, a feeling, maybe some griping.
turns.zh: 我当时当然以为这只是一种观察、一种感受，也许只是些抱怨。

turns.en: But when I left, went back and looked at track records other than ours and looked at what would be likely in different products, it was exceptionally true.
turns.zh: 但等我回去以后，看了看除我们自己之外其他人的历史业绩记录，又研究了在不同产品里可能会出现的情况，发现这确实异常真实。

turns.en: And the early industry at the time I don't think was as sensitive to some professional allocators needs for the fact that when there was when once they took positions, when there was rising volatility, which oftentimes was accompanied by rising correlation
turns.zh: 而且当时的早期行业，我认为对一些专业配置者的需求并没有那么敏感——也就是这样的事实：一旦他们建立了头寸，当波动率上升时（这往往伴随着相关性上升），

turns.en: that the overall net exposure was rising and that it wasn't poor timing, but that a reversal in some cases was approximately three or four times faster in equity. P and L. I don't think you see that in track records today because in the early 2000s many people, including ourselves, began volatility targeting the portfolio or volatility targeting segments of the portfolio to Mute those kinds of responses to make it more compatible with professional allocators dedicating
turns.zh: 整体净敞口是在上升的，而且这并不是糟糕的择时，而是说在某些情况下，权益的盈亏（P&L）反转大约快三四倍。我想你在今天的业绩记录里看不到这种情况了，因为在 2000 年代初，很多人（包括我们自己）开始对组合、或对组合的某些部分做波动率目标化（volatility targeting），以抑制这类反应，让它更能契合专业配置者去投入

turns.en: exposure. Interesting. I mean it is a topic that we've had on in different guises over the years fall targeting or not or should even the kind of the idea of pure trend versus more diversified systems.
turns.zh: 敞口的做法。有意思。我的意思是，这确实是一个我们这些年以不同形式讨论过的话题：要不要做波动率目标化，甚至包括纯趋势（pure trend）与更分散化系统之间的这种理念之争。

turns.en: It sounds like from your perspective that you do really have to solve for investor needs.
turns.zh: 听起来从你的角度看，你确实必须去解决投资者的需求。

turns.en: More so than shooting for the Maxon Rayrock. I think it's the only way you can go. I mean, I've had investors, savvy investors who I remember, I remember getting a call when they, when they would call and double the size of their account.
turns.zh: 而不是一味去追求最高的 RAROC。我觉得这是你唯一能走的路。我是说，我有过一些投资者、老练的投资者，我记得——我记得接到过他们的电话，他们会打电话过来把自己账户的规模翻倍。

turns.en: I was almost certain that that was the end of any industry drawdown. They were so good at it or when they took half off the table
turns.zh: 那时我几乎可以肯定，那就是整个行业回撤（drawdown）的终点了。他们在这方面太在行了；或者当他们把一半资金撤出、落袋为安时，

turns.en: that, you know, essentially it was time that the current party of the day was over.
turns.zh: 你知道，那基本就意味着当下这场“当日派对”该结束了。

turns.en: There were others that could never find that sense of value in investing.
turns.zh: 还有些人始终无法在投资中找到那种价值感。

turns.en: It's the usual tragedy of managed money to watch people watch performance, wait for there to be enough confirmation and confidence, get in a little bit too late and put themselves on a right shift of time off cycle.
turns.zh: 这就是受托资金管理常见的悲剧：眼睁睁看着大家盯着业绩，等到有足够的确认和信心才进场，结果进得稍微晚了点，把自己放到了一个错开周期的时间右移上。

turns.en: It doesn't really matter if you're taking outside money. I still think you just have to do the best job for every single allocation that you have.
turns.zh: 其实你收不收外部资金并不重要。我仍然认为，你就是得为你手上的每一笔配置都做到最好。

turns.en: But by no means, I think, can you group them all in the same bucket. They really, I think, have idiosyncratic and important differences in their organizations for how they've designed their portfolio, how they consider your contribution, how they even capitalize that contribution.
turns.zh: 但我认为，你绝对不能把他们全都归到同一个筐里。他们在各自的组织方式上真的存在特有的、重要的差异：他们如何设计自己的组合、如何看待你的贡献、甚至如何为那份贡献定价。

turns.en: Things that I know you both are very expert at. Can I, can I jump in here in this particular topic? Sorry to do that, Alan, but, but here's something interesting
turns.zh: 这些我都知道你们两位都非常在行。我能不能、能不能在这个话题上插一句？抱歉啊 Alan，不过这里有件有意思的事。

turns.en: I think we've heard from many industries, and I certainly remember from conversations that I've had with our colleagues in the industry
turns.zh: 我想我们从很多行业里都听到过，而且我当然记得从我与业内同行的一些谈话中——

turns.en: that I think people would question that customers or clients actually know what product is best, if I can define it like that.
turns.zh: 我认为人们会质疑：客户或委托人是否真的知道什么产品才是最好的，如果我可以这么界定的话。

turns.en: And so I think I know what, what, what you're referring to, Pat. And I think from a purely business perspective, clearly if you only have products nobody wants to buy, there's no use in that.
turns.zh: 所以我想我明白你指的是什么了，Pat。我认为从纯粹的商业角度看，显然如果你手上的产品没人想买，那也没什么用。

turns.en: On the other hand, I think our industry as trend followers, it's probably not the most liked investment strategy out there, but it offers tremendous value.
turns.zh: 但另一方面，我认为我们这个作为趋势跟踪者的行业，它大概不是市面上最受喜爱的投资策略，但它提供了巨大的价值。

turns.en: But I think part of that value actually comes from us doing it the way we think is the right way to do it.
turns.zh: 但我认为，那份价值有一部分其实来自我们按照自己认为正确的方式去做。

turns.en: And then the data will support investors making allocation to it.
turns.zh: 然后数据就会支持投资者去配置它。

turns.en: So I don't know if I misunderstood what you were saying on or whether you agree that Certainly if we're just talking about pure trend, we can get to how you can diversify away from trend in a second. But certainly if you think about pure trend, it's probably not going to have the profile that most investors says, yeah, I love that shape of the return stream.
turns.zh: 所以我不知道是不是我误解了你的意思，还是你是否同意：当然，如果我们只谈纯趋势——我们可以稍后再讲你如何从趋势中做分散化——但如果你想的是纯趋势，它大概不会具备那种让大多数投资者会说“是啊，我太喜欢这种回报流的形态了”的特征。

turns.en: But on the other hand, it's an incredibly useful property to have in, in a traditional portfolio. Do you know what I mean?
turns.zh: 但另一方面，在一个传统的组合里，它是一种极其有用的属性。你明白我的意思吗？

turns.en: I not only know what you mean, but let me take it a little further and see if you agree.
turns.zh: 我不仅明白你的意思，而且让我再往前推一步，看看你同不同意。

turns.en: When I say there's a moral difference of understanding the client's goals, I use those words on purpose because what the client exactly wants isn't necessarily always what their goals are.
turns.zh: 当我说存在一种理解客户目标的道德区别时，我是刻意用这些词的，因为客户究竟想要什么，并不总是等同于他们的目标。

turns.en: And I think there's a listening phase there. And one of the most pernicious and damaging things I think traders have done to themselves is to respond to marketing feedback in the hopes of growing their business.
turns.zh: 我认为这其中有一个倾听的阶段。而且我觉得交易员对自己做过的最有害、最具破坏性的事情之一，就是为了把生意做大而去迎合市场的反馈。

turns.en: They end up changing what they do. And if we rolled back the clock 30 or 40 years, there would not be 20 page pitch decks. If you were interviewing a trader, the four seminal questions were always what's your edge in the marketplace?
turns.zh: 他们最后改变了自己所做的事情。如果把时钟倒回三四十年前，那时候可没有 20 页的路演材料（pitch deck）。如果你要面试一名交易员，那四个最核心的问题永远是：你在市场上的优势（edge）是什么？

turns.en: How and where are you going to exploit that edge? What is your risk management or position sizing?
turns.zh: 你打算如何、在哪里去利用这个优势？你的风险管理或头寸规模（position sizing）是怎样的？

turns.en: And just when you thought you were done with the interview, the last question was and how do you protect your tails?
turns.zh: 而就在你以为面试快结束的时候，最后一个问题是：你如何保护自己的尾部风险（tails）？

turns.en: And the minute. And trend followers have done it. Hedge funds have done it. It's, it's pervasive. Private equity groups have done it.
turns.zh: 而一旦……趋势跟踪者干过这事，对冲基金也干过，这非常普遍，私募股权（private equity）机构也干过。

turns.en: They get into the marketplace, they hear some feedback and they start to try to change what they do.
turns.zh: 他们进入市场，听到一些反馈，就开始试图改变自己做的事情。

turns.en: And a trend follower has a very, a pure, I think the way you use the term, a pure trend follower has a very specific edge
turns.zh: 而一名趋势跟踪者拥有一个非常——用你的说法，一个纯粹的（pure）趋势跟踪者——拥有一个非常具体的优势，

turns.en: from agnosticism. And there are nuances along the way, but for the most part the setup, the signal, the position sizing, the asymmetry of positions, all of those things rely upon multi asset class, multidirectional participation.
turns.zh: 这种优势来自一种“不可知论”（agnosticism）。这一路上会有一些细微差别，但大体而言，入场设置、信号、头寸规模、头寸的不对称性，所有这些都依赖于跨多资产类别、多方向的参与。

turns.en: You get, you offer the client the ability for them as they're invested in singular asset classes long, you offer them the possibility as capital moves from one asset class to another, from one sub asset group to another, from another, from long to short, from long to flat, from selling one to buying another, which inherently of course is obviously a synthetic short and long.
turns.zh: 你——你为客户提供这样一种能力：当他们做多单一资产类别时，你为他们提供这样一种可能性——随着资本从一个资产类别转移到另一个、从一个子资产组转移到另一个、从做多转为做空、从做多转为平仓、从卖出一种转为买入另一种，而这本质上当然显然是一种合成的做空与做多。

turns.en: You are picking up return as that capital moves over months and quarters.
turns.zh: 随着资本在数月、数季度间流转，你就在其中获取回报。

turns.en: It brings the convexity that is so valuable, it brings the skew that's so valuable, at least on the timeframe of quarterly and semiannually, which is another discussion of how those terms are sometimes confused and you know, if there's a reflexivity in the marketplace in pricing, which is strong, and there is, there's still a reflexivity in the managed money business of, of managers conforming to what they think clients need and then clients changing what they want based on what they think they heard managers evolving
turns.zh: 它带来了那种极其宝贵的凸性（convexity），带来了那种极其宝贵的偏度（skew），至少是在季度和半年度这样的时间框架上——关于这些术语有时如何被混淆，那又是另一个话题了。你知道，如果市场定价中存在一种反身性（reflexivity），而且它很强，确实存在，那么在受托资金管理这行里仍然还有一种反身性：管理者去迎合他们认为客户需要的东西，然后客户又根据他们以为听到的、管理者正在演化的方向，去改变自己想要的东西。

turns.en: to. And I think the true north compass needs to always come back. Is there a market edge? Because if it starts to drift from that edge, results are just going to get worse.
turns.zh: 我认为那根指向正北的罗盘始终要回到这个问题上：是否存在市场优势（market edge）？因为一旦它开始偏离那个优势，结果只会越来越糟。

turns.en: Yeah, you mentioned a few S's there. I think we probably should dive down maybe a little bit further
turns.zh: 是的，你刚才提到了几个“S”。我想我们也许应该再往下深入一点，

turns.en: into those S's, because I think one of the things that I hope
turns.zh: 深入这几个“S”里去，因为我觉得我希望我们今天能做到的事情之一，

turns.en: we're going to do today is also to kind of get your take on the narrative side. I think this is something we've talked about for years, how difficult it has been for our industry to really maybe explain well enough the benefits and so on and so forth.
turns.zh: 也是听听你在叙事（narrative）这一面的看法。我想这是我们谈论多年的一个话题：我们这个行业要真正把种种好处解释清楚，一直有多么困难，等等等等。

turns.en: We know narrative is incredibly important, but maybe we could just start with the kind of the four S's that you referred to and take it from there.
turns.zh: 我们知道叙事极其重要，但也许我们可以先从你提到的那“四个 S”开始，然后再往下展开。

turns.en: Well, you know, the four S's is a helpful. It's not a complete framework, but it's a helpful starting framework for anyone who wishes to trade in that.
turns.zh: 嗯，你知道，这“四个 S”很有用。它不是一个完整的框架，但对任何想在这方面做交易的人来说，它是一个很有用的起步框架。

turns.en: It's part of the mechanism. It's not really part of, I think, of a grander narrative. We probably should park that for a separate question.
turns.zh: 它是机制的一部分。我认为它并不真正属于一个更宏大的叙事，那个我们大概应该留到一个单独的问题里再谈。

turns.en: But if somebody's trying to set up a successful trading approach, and it probably works for discretionary, systematic or both, but let's just confine it to systematic for now.
turns.zh: 但如果有人想搭建一套成功的交易方法，它大概对主观（discretionary）、系统化（systematic）或两者都适用，不过我们暂时就把它限定在系统化上。

turns.en: Normally the four S's would need to be satisfied. You simply have to ask yourself, what is the setup for your trades?
turns.zh: 通常这四个 S 都需要被满足。你只需问问自己：你交易的入场设置（setup）是什么？

turns.en: Are you trading continuously? Or is there some form of a setup you're looking for that raises your probability in a, in a Bayesian sense for when you wish to, to exploit your edge.
turns.zh: 你是在持续不断地交易，还是有某种形式的入场设置是你在寻找的，它能在贝叶斯（Bayesian）意义上提高你的概率，以便在你想要利用自己优势的时候？

turns.en: 2 2nds, what's your signal? What makes you get in? What makes you get out?
turns.zh: 第二，你的信号（signal）是什么？是什么让你进场？是什么让你出场？

turns.en: Three, what's your sizing? This is sort of synonymous with risk management, but I'm sizing now includes forward opportunity and risk.
turns.zh: 第三，你的规模（sizing）是怎样的？这在某种意义上等同于风险管理，但我说的规模如今还包含了未来的机会与风险。

turns.en: And then two, what's your symmetry? Have you entered a trade with an equal window loss, balance, or have you entered a trade either directly or synthetically, where you have an asymmetric advantage?
turns.zh: 然后再一个，你的对称性（symmetry）如何？你进入一笔交易时是盈亏窗口对等的平衡状态，还是你直接或合成地进入了一笔交易、从而拥有不对称的优势？

turns.en: And that's what I really meant by the four S's. I think those are more of a practice, a discipline of understanding how to put together a trading system that has well defined steps and, and there's an infinite number of those solutions perhaps, but the better defined they are.
turns.zh: 这才是我说“四个 S”真正想表达的意思。我认为它们更多的是一种实践、一种纪律，去理解如何搭建一个有着清晰界定步骤的交易系统；这样的解法也许有无数种，但它们界定得越清楚，

turns.en: And I think if a trader or an investor soul searches their answer to each one and understands why they're doing it, they will also

turns.en: And we had met him once. Then we met him a second time. And I still remember him saying something to the effect of
turns.zh: 我们此前见过他一次，然后又见了第二次。我至今还记得他说的话，大意是——

turns.zh: “Pat，我们的成功与别人之间的区别在于，我们是真正遵循自己的系统的。”

turns.zh: 然后我还记得他说的另一件事：我们大可以把我们的系统印在 Highway 101 的一块广告牌上，也完全不用担心什么，因为没人会去遵循它——因为它不是他们自己的，他们对它不会有信心。

turns.en: Which really means you have to, you know, the trader or the investor and the methodology, they have to pair themselves with a degree of confidence or there's really no way to exploit that edge through time.

turns.en: But because it's, I think, a relatively.

turns.zh: 它既不带情绪，也不依附于任何关于成功的道理，更多的是些干巴巴的事实，谈不上什么说服力。

turns.en: I don't think over time, there's been very many compelling matches between an investor and a manager based strictly on what do I do every single day, what math do I invoke, what formulas do I use.
turns.zh: 我不认为长期以来，投资者与管理人之间有过很多真正打动人的匹配，是严格建立在“我每天做什么、我用什么数学、我用什么公式”之上的。

turns.en: I think for the most part, they're either unappreciated, unmoved, or quickly forgotten.
turns.zh: 我认为大多数情况下，这些东西要么不被欣赏，要么让人无动于衷，要么很快就被忘掉。

turns.en: So I'm curious about your thoughts on replication. Well, I think I would separate replication from the mechanism of replicating and versus the productizing of replication.
turns.zh: 所以我很好奇你怎么看复制这件事。嗯，我想我会把“复制”这件事，与“复制的机制”以及“复制的产品化”分开来看。

turns.en: I think one of those is a, is a valid mathematical way of formulating a systematic approach and it's something that almost every trader does one way or another.
turns.zh: 我认为其中一个是构建系统化方法的一种有效的数学方式，而且几乎每个交易员都以某种方式在做这件事。

turns.en: Even a trend follower, for instance, does not trade primary cash bonds or primary cash commodities mano a mano with other counterparties when they're really waiting for price, smoothing price and deciding some formulaic way of deciding whether to say there's an uptrend or a downtrend that's really replicating the actions of others through the reflection of the information of the price signal, which is then typically smoothed and brought in.
turns.zh: 举例来说，即便是趋势跟踪者，也不会与其他对手方一对一地去交易一级市场的现券或现货商品——当他们其实是在等待价格、盯着价格，用某种公式化的方式去判断该说这是上升趋势还是下降趋势时，那其实就是在通过价格信号所反映的信息去复制他人的行为，而这个信号通常还会被平滑处理后再纳入。

turns.en: There's not much of a different step to then say the P and L of another trader is now just a price signal that then is used to replicate, usually by some form of regression technique
turns.zh: 从这里再往前一步也差不了多少，就是说：另一名交易员的盈亏（P&L）现在只是一个价格信号，然后被用来做复制，通常是通过某种形式的回归（regression）技术。

turns.en: where it's done and it's been done in many, many areas. I mean I, I don't think any of your sophisticated audience would,
turns.zh: 这在很多很多领域都在做、也已经做过。我是说，我不认为你们那些老练的听众中会有谁，

turns.en: would be surprised to learn that AN S&P 500 Index Fund doesn't have to own all 500 stocks at any given point in time to replicate the S&P 500.
turns.zh: 在得知一只 S&P 500 指数基金在任何一个时点都不必持有全部 500 只股票就能复制 S&P 500 时，会感到惊讶。

turns.en: So I just separate that because we've actually done some very specific work to replicate some of the replicators, mainly to ask our own questions. We wanted to see what are some of the reduced minimal market set sizes that replicate say the trend following industry.
turns.zh: 所以我只是把这一点分开来说，因为我们其实做过一些非常具体的工作，去复制那些“复制者”，主要是为了问我们自己的一些问题。我们想看看，比如说要复制整个趋势跟踪行业，那种经过精简的、最小的市场集合规模会是多大。

turns.en: Is it similar, for instance, in some of the popular ETFs that are used?
turns.zh: 比如说，它跟一些被广泛使用的热门 ETF 是不是相似？

turns.en: Some of those ETFs have changed their market set over times. If they hadn't, would there have been much of a change?
turns.zh: 其中一些 ETF 随着时间改变过它们的市场集合。如果它们没改，那还会有多大变化吗？

turns.en: There would not have been. By the way, if we do replicate the replicators, we actually end up with better performance.
turns.zh: 不会有。顺便说一句，如果我们真去复制那些“复制者”，我们最终得到的业绩反而更好。

turns.en: But that's probably not too surprising because we end up with a little better smoothing coefficient and we have probably end up with less churn for rebalances at the end of the day. And, and if it were fully funded, you'd have probably lower fees and better cash management.
turns.zh: 但这大概也不算太令人意外，因为我们最终得到的拟合系数（fitting coefficient）会稍好一些，而且说到底，我们在再平衡（rebalance）上的换手（churn）大概也更少。如果它是全额出资的，你大概还会得到更低的费用和更好的现金管理。

turns.en: So if an institution wants to do $500 million. They don't necessarily have to go into a retail product and they could get the same idea.
turns.zh: 所以如果一家机构想投 5 亿美元，他们不一定非得去买一个零售产品，他们可以获得同样的思路。

turns.en: The other part of replication, of course, is sort of the less savory part.
turns.zh: 当然，复制的另一部分，就是那种不那么光彩的部分了。

turns.en: It's the narrative story. It's the hero's journey, if you will.
turns.zh: 那是叙事的故事，如果你愿意这么说的话，是那种“英雄之旅”（hero's journey）。

turns.en: Somebody has to come along and you know, solve the problem. You know, the, the rapacious managers are charging too much money, they're too opaque and we're going to beat them at their own game and we're going to sell this much lower, et cetera, et cetera.
turns.zh: 总得有人站出来，你知道，去解决这个问题。你懂的，那些贪婪的管理人收费太高、太不透明，而我们要在他们自己的游戏里打败他们，我们要以低得多的价格来卖这个东西，等等等等。

turns.en: And you know, it certainly worked for Jack Bogle. He wasn't in the hedge fund world. He was trying to give consumers a better deal.
turns.zh: 你知道，这一套对 Jack Bogle 来说当然奏效了。他不在对冲基金那个世界里，他是想给消费者一个更划算的选择。

turns.en: It starts to stretch though, as you get more and more into the very, very active ETFs.
turns.zh: 不过，随着你越来越深入到那些非常非常主动的 ETF 里，这就开始变得牵强了。

turns.en: At some point that gets to be a fuzzy margin of extracting cost, which is clearly true when you have a three or five basis point product or whether or not you're simply trying to carve another narrative niche out and finding a sensitivity point.
turns.zh: 到了某个点，这就成了一个模糊的“提取成本”边界——当你有一个三到五个基点（basis point）的产品时，这一点显然成立；又或者你只是想再切出一个叙事上的细分定位、找到一个能戳中人的敏感点。

turns.en: And some allocators, the overall cost or the manager selection risk, those are two failure points for some of the professional allocation stabs that exist in the world. So solving for those two would definitely appeal to a large number of people.
turns.zh: 而且对一些配置者来说，总体成本或者管理人选择风险（manager selection risk），这是世上一些专业配置尝试中的两个失败点。所以解决了这两点，肯定会吸引很多人。

turns.zh: 好的，Alan，抱歉我刚才把话题给劫持了。是啊，我只是好奇，你知道，你显然在市场里待了很多年，我想你说过你是从大学时就开始做交易的，然后你把很大一部分重心放在趋势跟踪上——Hunt Brothers 白银

turns.en: Trade, my first trade. Okay, so here you go. But you've, you've, you've had programs in kind of quant macro type program, short term equity.
turns.zh: 那笔交易，是我的第一笔交易。好，那你说吧。不过你做过一些量化宏观（quant macro）类型的程序、短期股票

Was it an observation on behavior or just an observation on what works or something that has just evolved the markets and what underpins that to give you confidence that these types of strategies will continue to work going forward?
turns.zh: 你知道，我只是好奇你关于市场与投资的那套哲学是从哪儿来的。它是源于对行为的观察，还是仅仅源于对“什么管用”的观察，或者是随着市场演化而来的东西？而支撑这一切、让你有信心认为这类策略未来会继续管用的又是什么？

turns.en: Yeah, I think that goes back to Niall's question of if we were to want to improve our narrative, at least for some classes of investors, would we stay with the true statement that trends are behavioral, but then be willing to defend the fact that the non trending periods are also behavioral and the periods of high liquidity are behavioral and the periods of low liquidity are behavioral because the markets are the sum of the participant behaviors.
turns.zh: 是的，我想这要回到 Niels 的那个问题：如果我们想改善我们的叙事，至少对某几类投资者而言，我们是否会坚持“趋势是行为性的”这个真实的论断，但同时愿意去捍卫这样一个事实——非趋势的时期同样是行为性的，高流动性的时期是行为性的，低流动性的时期也是行为性的，因为市场就是所有参与者行为的总和。

turns.en: All true. I think sometimes those kinds of explanations just simply aren't enough for the types of people who are listening who either if they've had sort of CFA and securities training, they're listening one way.
turns.zh: 这些都对。我认为有时候这类解释，对那些正在听的人来说根本不够——如果他们受过 CFA 和证券方面的训练，他们会以一种方式去听；

turns.en: If they've been entrepreneurs or it's family office wealth, they're listening from a different point of view.
turns.zh: 如果他们是企业家、或者是家族办公室（family office）财富，他们又会从另一个角度去听。

turns.en: Perhaps if they've had technical or engineering type backgrounds, they're listening from yet another point of view.
turns.zh: 也许如果他们是技术或工程类背景，他们又会从再另一个角度去听。

turns.en: And I think that it took 10 or 20 years of a lot of disciplined work and especially as we began trading for individual clients, a volatility arb program. We traded a stat arb program, thousands of trades per day.
turns.zh: 我认为这花了十到二十年大量有纪律的工作，尤其是当我们开始为个人客户交易一个波动率套利（volatility arb）程序时。我们交易过一个统计套利（stat arb）程序，每天成千上万笔交易。

turns.en: For a while we've traded trend following. Really to come back and say, I think the best narrative after some form of a story, of a character overcoming a challenge,
turns.zh: 我们也做趋势跟踪有一段时间了。真的，回过头来说，我认为在某种“一个角色克服挑战”的故事之后，最好的叙事，

turns.en: that's the thin layer. The next layer I think comes with, can you really tell me where the returns source from?
turns.zh: 那只是薄薄的一层。我认为下一层随之而来的是：你能不能真正告诉我，这些回报究竟源自哪里？

turns.zh: 我是市场的一名学生。这些回报是从哪来的？而我认为，从趋势跟踪来看，

turns.en: We've been quite successful decomposing trend returns into true counterparts. I think that there are four.
turns.zh: 我们在把趋势回报分解成真正的构成部分方面做得相当成功。我认为有四个。

turns.en: If we stick truly with trend following, which I'm going to define now, says holding positions through time for a profit. I didn't say long or short, I didn't say one. I just said holding positions through time with one more feature, some form of buying strength and selling weakness.
turns.zh: 如果我们真正坚持趋势跟踪——我现在就给它下个定义——它说的是随时间持有头寸以获利。我没说是做多还是做空，也没说是哪一个方向。我只是说随时间持有头寸，再加上一个特征：某种形式的买入强势、卖出弱势。

turns.en: That's what the following part means. We're not predicting. I think one can decompose returns into the components of economic trend, into financial carry, into information diffusion and then into some form of reflexivity in a Sorosian term or in an academic term, or just a feedback loop.
turns.zh: 这就是“跟踪”（following）那部分的含义：我们不是在做预测。我认为你可以把回报分解成这几个组成部分：经济趋势（economic trend）、金融套息（financial carry）、信息扩散（information diffusion），然后是某种形式的反身性——用 Soros 式的术语、或用学术术语来说，或者就干脆说是一个反馈回路（feedback loop）。

turns.en: Buying begets buying. Each of those, it's different powers in different sectors.
turns.zh: 买入催生更多买入。这几者中的每一个，在不同的板块里都有着不同的力量。

turns.en: They have different time frames and clocks. And when I talk to investors and they need a natural metaphor, it's not a stretch for them to say, look, if you had a boat in the ocean, there isn't one source.
turns.zh: 它们有着不同的时间框架和节奏。当我和投资者交谈、而他们需要一个自然的比喻时，对他们来说这么讲并不牵强：瞧，如果你在大洋上有一条船，推动它的并不是单一来源。

turns.en: The boat will move because it's in a current. The boat will also move because it's in a tide.
turns.zh: 船会因为处在洋流（current）中而移动，也会因为处在潮汐（tide）中而移动。

turns.en: The boat will move because a wind is applied to it. A boat may also move because someone starts an engine.
turns.zh: 船会因为风作用在它上面而移动，也可能因为有人发动了引擎而移动。

turns.en: Now all those could all be in the same direction. They could be in the opposite direction. You could have a positive economic carry, for instance, in
turns.zh: 而所有这些都可能是同一个方向的，也可能是相反方向的。比如说，你可能有一个正向的经济套息——在

turns.en: equity indices, which is extremely strong, but have face for the most of the time a negative financial carry and still come out of head in something that has very little influence of a long term economic carry, but a strong financial carry.
turns.zh: 股票指数上，它极其强劲，但在大部分时间里却要面对一个负的金融套息，可最终仍能保持领先——在某个受长期经济套息影响很小、但金融套息很强的东西上。

turns.en: One could look at say roll premium and fixed income contracts.
turns.zh: 比如说，你可以看看固定收益合约里的展期溢价（roll premium）。

turns.en: If one does a pretty careful decomposition of trend, one will find that the majority, and in some cases the vast majority of returns will be accumulated term structure, premium, not so true in other markets.
turns.zh: 如果一个人对趋势做一次相当细致的分解，他会发现，大部分——在某些情况下是绝大部分——的回报来自累积的期限结构溢价（term structure premium），这在其他市场里就不那么成立了。

turns.en: But those four components, I think way beyond the scope of our one hour podcast.
turns.zh: 但那四个组成部分，我想远远超出了我们这档一小时播客的范围。

turns.en: We could spend entire times decomposing returns and showing those return decompositions and why a trend follower picks them up and why a trend follower picks them up agnostically. Because they do flex, they do change, and they can have unexpected directionality.
turns.zh: 我们完全可以花上整段时间去分解回报、展示这些回报分解，讲清楚为什么趋势跟踪者能获取它们、以及为什么趋势跟踪者是以一种“不可知”的方式去获取它们的。因为它们确实会伸缩、会变化，而且可能有着出乎意料的方向性。

turns.en: There's a great story of 2013. I remember 2013 is not unlike a little bit today in that everyone, everyone was writing how much bonds will go up and how much interest rates will go up.
turns.zh: 有一个关于 2013 年的很好的故事。我记得 2013 年在某种程度上跟今天有点像，因为当时每个人、每个人都在写债券会涨多少、利率会升多少。

turns.en: And to get ready and of course what happened in 2014? Interest rates went down the entire year and Trend followers made 20 or 30% and almost everybody else missed on their predictions, but they were still happy because if they own bonds, they went up.
turns.zh: 让大家做好准备。可结果 2014 年发生了什么？利率整整一年都在下行，趋势跟踪者赚了 20% 或 30%，而几乎其他所有人的预测都错了——但他们仍然很开心，因为如果他们持有债券，债券涨了。

turns.en: So trend following has a very powerful meta cognition of all these returns. But I think if you're trying to explain it and the person has an economics or investment background, showing the return attributions plainly that they could even derive on their own, or they can see how they are derived independently from the opinion of the trader.
turns.zh: 所以趋势跟踪对所有这些回报有一种非常强大的元认知（meta cognition）。但我认为，如果你想解释它，而对方又有经济学或投资背景，那就把回报归因（return attribution）清清楚楚地展示出来——他们甚至能自己推导出来，或者能看到这些归因是如何独立于交易员的个人观点被推导出来的。

turns.en: I've seen light bulbs go off in people's head like why didn't somebody just show me this years ago?
turns.zh: 我见过人们脑子里“灵光一现”的样子，就像在说：为什么多年前没人直接把这个展示给我看？

turns.en: Now I get it. And they get everything. They get why the correlation is zero, they get why it's positively convex.
turns.zh: “现在我懂了。”于是他们什么都懂了：他们懂了为什么相关性是零，懂了为什么它是正向凸性的。

turns.en: All kinds of things happen positively. And that kind of high level justification, you think that's the same to different degrees. I mean, maybe you might weigh those four factors differently for say short term trend following or systematic macro signals.
turns.zh: 各种事情都会朝好的方向发生。那么那种高层次的论证，你觉得它在不同程度上是一样的吗？我是说，也许对于比如短期趋势跟踪或系统化宏观信号，你会给那四个因素不同的权重？

turns.en: I think the answer is true in both cases. So almost by definition something that is some form of a carry, like an economic carry or a financial carry, I'm essentially saying something that those positions benefit by time.
turns.zh: 我认为这个答案在两种情况下都成立。所以几乎是按定义来说，某种形式的套息（carry）——比如经济套息或金融套息——我本质上是在说，这些头寸会因时间而获益。

turns.en: Your ownership through time is what accrues profits. So if I make something short term, I'm essentially taking those out of the equation.
turns.zh: 你随时间推移的持有权，才是累积利润的来源。所以如果我把某个东西做成短期的，我本质上就是把那些因素从等式里拿掉了。

turns.en: Back to a water analogy. If I'm, if I'm, if I'm swimming downstream in a river, I can swim faster with the carry than I'm swimming upstream against the carry.
turns.zh: 回到水的比喻。如果我、如果我、如果我在河里顺流而游，我借助这股水流能游得比逆流而上顶着水流更快。

turns.en: That will matter if I'm swimming for 20 hours. If I'm swimming for three seconds, the carry doesn't matter very much.
turns.zh: 如果我要游 20 个小时，这一点就很重要。但如果我只游 3 秒钟，那这股水流就不太重要了。

turns.en: So short term definitely spends more time not only in the information diffusion and reflexivity, but it also begins to pick up other terms I didn't include in trend following because the impact of flows, accelerating flows, periodic flows, rebalancing flows, these Kinds of, these kinds of more market mechanistic I think are far more useful in the time frames of say less than 10 day holding periods.
turns.zh: 所以短期交易肯定会花更多时间不仅在信息扩散和反身性上，它还会开始捕捉一些我在趋势跟踪里没有纳入的其他项，因为资金流（flows）的影响——加速的资金流、周期性的资金流、再平衡的资金流——这些更偏市场机制层面的东西，我认为在比如说持有期少于 10 天这样的时间框架里要有用得多。

turns.en: As a matter of fact, there have been very few instances except for very large contracts, large dollar volatility of the contracts, oftentimes with large point values in those contracts where you can parameterize any type of a traditional trend following mechanistic approach and make money with very short term holding periods.
turns.zh: 事实上，除了那些非常大的合约——那些合约的美元波动率很大、往往点值（point value）也很大——之外，几乎没有几个例子，能让你把任何类型的传统趋势跟踪机制化方法参数化，然后用非常短的持有期还能赚到钱。

turns.en: Three days, four days, five days. Even in academic studies when they look at short term trend following, usually the holding periods are closer to a month on average.
turns.zh: 三天、四天、五天。即便是在学术研究中，当他们研究短期趋势跟踪时，持有期通常平均也接近一个月。

turns.en: There's just a very narrow window where by the time you buy strength and sell weakness, what's left in the middle is your potential profit. And if you're only in the market for three days or six or five,
turns.zh: 只有一个非常狭窄的窗口：等你买入强势、卖出弱势之后，中间剩下的才是你的潜在利润。而如果你只在市场里待三天、六天或五天，

turns.en: other techniques work better. And, and we've learned that and experienced that, but we've also focused a lot on it.
turns.zh: 那么其他技术会更管用。这一点我们学到过、也亲身经历过，但我们在这方面也投入了很多精力。

turns.en: We love trend following, it works. We love macro systematic macro trading because it works. And what I mean by that in this case definitionally is a full separation trend uses price. The macro trading uses only cross asset signals, fundamental signals, government reports, alternative data, the short term data, the short term models are all principally focused on flows with holding periods far less than 10 days typically.
turns.zh: 我们热爱趋势跟踪，因为它管用。我们也热爱系统化宏观交易（systematic macro trading），因为它管用。而在这里，我从定义上说指的是二者的完全分离：趋势用的是价格；宏观交易只用跨资产信号、基本面信号、政府报告、另类数据（alternative data）；短期数据、短期模型则主要聚焦于资金流，持有期通常远少于 10 天。

turns.en: And in our particular firm we also would include things like relative value trading where we are very specifically trying to create neutralized baskets that are really helpful to our main portfolio, a main portfolio and macro or in managed futures some will pick up large scale thematic risks, direction of U.S. interest rates, direction of U.S. equities, direction of energies.
turns.zh: 在我们这家公司里，我们还会纳入诸如相对价值交易（relative value trading）这样的东西，在这里我们非常明确地试图构建一些中性化的篮子（neutralized baskets），它们对我们的主组合真正有帮助。一个主组合，在宏观或 managed futures 里，会去承接一些大规模的主题性风险——美国利率的方向、美国股票的方向、能源的方向。

turns.en: And there's a natural construction where you can build say a dollar neutral currency basket. Now you're not stacking on top of your dollar risk. You can pick a, a rate neutral interest rate basket and you're not stacking on your DVO1 or commodity neutral basket.
turns.zh: 而且有一种自然的构建方式，你可以搭建比如说一个美元中性（dollar neutral）的货币篮子，这样你就不会在自己的美元风险上层层加码。你可以挑一个利率中性（rate neutral）的利率篮子，这样你就不会在自己的 DV01 上叠加；或者一个商品中性（commodity neutral）的篮子，

turns.en: And you're not just landing on top of broad based. So that adds diversification and I guess as long as I'm actually addressing it. The fifth thing that we do in our multi strategy is a dedicated risk off sleeve which is only designed to sell equities.
turns.zh: 你就不会正好压在广泛基准的风险之上。所以这增加了分散化。而且我想，既然我正聊到这个，我们在多策略里做的第五件事，是一个专门的风险规避（risk off）分支（sleeve），它的设计目的就是为了卖出股票。

turns.en: When there's a rapid rise in flow data that shows us to have hedging and mispricing activities.
turns.zh: 当资金流数据出现快速上升、向我们显示出存在对冲和错误定价（mispricing）活动的时候。

turns.en: When people are willing as an edge to give us money to neutralize the risk, our edge rises and it helps our clients.
turns.zh: 当人们愿意作为一种优势、把钱交给我们去中性化风险时，我们的优势就上升了，而且这也帮到了我们的客户。

turns.en: Now Pat, you mentioned yourself there the word multistrad. And of course we can see the rise of multi strategy funds in the past, call it 20 years, maybe even shorter than that and I was wondering because obviously my personal bias is trend following.
turns.zh: Pat，刚才你自己提到了“多策略”（multi-strat）这个词。当然，我们能看到多策略基金在过去——就算它 20 年吧，也许比这还短——的崛起。我在想，因为显然我个人的偏好是趋势跟踪。

turns.en: Have you noticed? And I guess maybe it goes into some of the great work that Alan has been talking about in terms of regimes. But do you think that multi strat funds at large and how they trade, and I'm not an expert in that, but it's not trend following, at least not all of it.
turns.zh: 你有没有注意到——我想这也许涉及到 Alan 一直在谈的、关于市场状态（regimes）的那些出色工作。但你觉得，整体而言多策略基金以及它们的交易方式——我在这方面不是专家，但那不是趋势跟踪，至少不全是——

turns.en: Do you think that that has had an impact on, let's call it microstructure
turns.zh: 你觉得这对——我们就叫它微观结构（microstructure）吧——

turns.en: in some ways that is reflected on trend following or does trend following actually by being adaptive in itself kind of find ways to compensate for it even though for short periods of time
turns.zh: 有没有产生过影响？这种影响在某些方面是否反映到了趋势跟踪上？还是说趋势跟踪其实凭着自身的适应性，多少找到了办法去抵消它，尽管在短时期内

turns.en: it may get affected? How do you see that? Yeah, this is the kind of subject matter that forms the basis of financial journalism. And then when one wants to really dive into it, it's harder to substantiate the information.
turns.zh: 它可能会受到影响？你怎么看？是的，这正是那种构成财经新闻基础的题材。可当一个人真想深入研究时，要去证实这些信息反而更难。

turns.en: I think. What do I think of multi strats? I think for the right clients they're a wonderful idea. I think many clients don't, don't have the skill or the time or the budget yet they have the desire to have a real alternative allocation and a vigorous sort of multi strategy product providers are there to provide it for good or for bad, expensive or cheap.
turns.zh: 我是这么想的。我怎么看多策略？我认为对于合适的客户来说，它们是个很棒的主意。我觉得很多客户并不具备相应的技能、时间或预算，却又渴望拥有一个真正的另类配置，而那些生机勃勃的多策略产品提供方就在那里提供它——无论是好是坏、是贵是廉。

turns.en: We're not really in that realm because we now only focus on futures and foreign exchange. So in our multi strategy approach is still at the more macro and individual derivative level. But I would say that's bullish for investors overall because I think all investors, if we looked at $100 trillion in allocatable capital around the world are massively under allocated to alternatives, not over.
turns.zh: 我们其实并不在那个领域里，因为我们现在只聚焦于期货和外汇。所以我们的多策略方法仍然处在更宏观、以及单个衍生品的层面上。但我会说，这对投资者整体是利好（bullish）的，因为我认为所有投资者——如果我们看看全球 100 万亿美元的可配置资本——对另类资产的配置是严重不足的，而不是过多。

turns.en: So that's going on. Sorry to interrupt here, Pat. Sorry to interrupt. My question was a little bit different. I think I was looking for, with your experience, the way you look at say being a trend follower for part of what you do, whether you think the size of these funds and the way they trade
turns.zh: 情况就是这样。抱歉在这里打断你，Pat，抱歉打断。我的问题其实有点不一样。我想问的是，以你的经验、以你把趋势跟踪作为你一部分工作的视角来看，你是否认为这些基金的规模以及它们的交易方式，

turns.en: has actually made it more difficult to be a trend follower. Meaning.
turns.zh: 实际上让做趋势跟踪变得更难了？意思是——

turns.en: No. Okay. No, not at all. I think the majority of hedge or of trend following returns are have been driven by accumulated economic and financial carries and information diffusion over months, if not semi annual to years.
turns.zh: 不。好。不，完全不是。我认为趋势跟踪回报的大部分，是由在数月、乃至半年到数年间累积的经济套息和金融套息、以及信息扩散所驱动的。

turns.en: None of which is definitely affected when you go into a ZIRP environment. It's definitely affected when spreads from in G7 environments all become extremely narrow and there's virtually no difference.
turns.zh: 当你进入零利率政策（ZIRP）环境时，这些并不会受到明确影响。而当 G7 环境里的利差全都变得极其狭窄、几乎没有差别时，它才会受到明确影响。

turns.en: These are massive differences for trend following. Yeah, not the type of trading.
turns.zh: 这些对趋势跟踪来说是巨大的差异。是的，而不是那种交易类型。

turns.en: I think a lot of the trading at the high leverage, shorter term, more arbitrage level is more in the concave surfaces of Markets
turns.zh: 我认为很多在高杠杆、更短期、更偏套利层面的交易，更多地处在市场的凹面（concave surfaces）上——

turns.en: that exist not just at the microstructure, which might be more
turns.zh: 这些凹面不仅存在于微观结构层面，那可能更偏向于

turns.en: market making, high frequency or the medium microstructure like say stat arb.
turns.zh: 做市（market making）、高频（high frequency），或者像统计套利那样的中等微观结构。

turns.en: If anything, for most trend followers it's either not seen or it may even be providing a liquidity pool.
turns.zh: 如果说有什么影响的话，对大多数趋势跟踪者而言，它要么根本看不到，要么甚至可能是在提供一个流动性池（liquidity pool）。

turns.en: True. Now before Alan jumps in, just one other thing. And of course I know you sense my distinct bias for trend following here, but I'm curious again, is there something you have heard
turns.zh: 没错。那么在 Alan 插话之前，还有一件事。当然，我知道你能感觉到我对趋势跟踪有明显的偏好，但我还是好奇：有没有什么你听到过的、

turns.en: being said about trend following that you really, I mean, what's the thing you disagree with the most when people kind of describe trend following?
turns.zh: 别人对趋势跟踪的说法，是你真的——我是说，当人们这样那样地描述趋势跟踪时，你最不认同的是哪一点？

turns.en: Oh boy. I'd love to give a clean answer, but I think it'll, it's, I'll be a slightly nuanced answer because it depends who's providing the criticism.
turns.zh: 哎呀。我很想给一个干净利落的回答，但我觉得这会是个稍微带点细微差别的回答，因为这取决于批评是谁提出的。

turns.en: Okay, so for instance, you know, I served wonderful with this, a wonderful man. So I served on a board with Bill Sharp for many years.
turns.zh: 好，那比如说，你知道，我曾与一位非常了不起的人共事。我在一个董事会里和 Bill Sharpe 一起共事了很多年。

turns.en: And someone like Bill Sharpe, he wouldn't necessarily have had a criticism of trend following.
turns.zh: 而像 Bill Sharpe 这样的人，他不一定会对趋势跟踪有什么批评。

turns.en: It would have been more like why bother? If you're going to invest for 20 years, you're going to invest in broad assets, own everything in the right proportion with the right growth because everything else at some point is noise.
turns.zh: 他的说法更像是：何必呢？如果你要投资 20 年，你就去投资广泛的资产，按合适的比例、合适的增长持有一切，因为其他所有东西到了某个点都是噪音。

turns.en: And that's simplified answer. That's not even a criticism. But that doesn't reflect the reality. As you know, if you go meet the allocation staff of a pension fund, if you go to a family office, if you, if you're on the other side of an endowment and their consultant has them in a particular allocation and somebody does a Monte Carlo analysis say on their pension assets and they find out that a, that a two sigma move on their pension plan might throw a $400 million liability onto
turns.zh: 那是个简化的回答，那甚至算不上批评。但它并不反映现实。你知道，如果你去见一家养老基金的配置团队，如果你去一个家族办公室，如果你站在一个捐赠基金（endowment）的另一端，而他们的顾问让他们维持某个特定的配置，然后有人对他们的养老资产做了一个蒙特卡洛（Monte Carlo）分析，他们发现其养老金计划上一个两倍标准差（two sigma）的波动，可能会给一家只有

turns.en: a company that's got 60 million in P and L and earnings and their head explodes. They need to have a better allocation strategically and one that can cover tail exposures better.
turns.zh: 6000 万盈亏和盈利的公司甩来 4 亿美元的负债，他们脑袋就炸了。他们在战略上需要一个更好的配置，一个能更好地覆盖尾部敞口（tail exposures）的配置。

turns.en: And I think then when you get to people who are living in a world where very adverse moves that occur over quarters or years matter to them, trend following becomes this invaluable tool if they use it right again, how one allocates capital to it, what's the opportunity cost to that capital?
turns.zh: 于是我认为，当你面对那些生活在一个“跨越数个季度或数年发生的不利波动对他们很重要”的世界里的人时，趋势跟踪就成了一件无比宝贵的工具——前提是他们用对了。同样地，一个人如何为它配置资本、那笔资本的机会成本是多少？

turns.en: Is it for instance, more like portable alpha? Is it fully allocated to at what volatility? These become all these mechanistic questions, but I don't think those criticisms are there.
turns.zh: 比如说，它更像是可携带阿尔法（portable alpha）吗？它是全额配置的吗？配置在什么波动率上？这些都成了各种机制层面的问题，但我不认为那些批评是成立的。

turns.en: The one criticism that not criticism but the one I remember I faced, it was again one of the popular financial press narratives.
turns.zh: 有一个批评——其实不算批评，而是我记得我面对过的一个，它又是那些流行的财经媒体叙事之一。

turns.en: I was giving a speech, I think at Pension Bridge. I'm not even sure if it was the same year I was on a panel with Katie Kaminsky, who is just such a wonderful joy and a bulient mind to be on a panel with.
turns.zh: 我当时在做一场演讲，我想是在 Pension Bridge。我甚至不确定是不是同一年，我和 Katie Kaminsky 一起参加了一个圆桌讨论——她真是一个极大的乐趣、一个才思敏捷的人，能和她同台真是荣幸。

turns.en: But it was one of those things where somebody in the audience asked me a question and they at the time it was are trend followers too big? Is there a capacity problem?
turns.zh: 但那是这样一种情形：观众里有人问了我一个问题，当时的问题是：趋势跟踪者是不是太大了？是否存在容量（capacity）问题？

turns.en: And I said, well, I'd like to just. I do this a lot with my graduate students and postdocs. Let's try a thought experiment and then we'll all decide at the end.
turns.zh: 我说，嗯，我想——我经常和我的研究生、博士后这么做——我们来做一个思想实验（thought experiment），最后大家再一起下结论。

turns.en: I said, what if before speaking here, I had gone to the private equity shops up in Embarcadero and others and I had arranged financing to do a roll up of all the Trend followers and CTAs that I could and I had billions of dollars to buy their businesses and I went around because I know them and called them and made them offers and the vast majority accepted and I now own 200 of the $250 billion worth of capacity.
turns.zh: 我说，如果在来这里演讲之前，我去找了 Embarcadero 上面那些私募股权机构以及其他地方，安排好了融资，去把我所能找到的所有趋势跟踪者和 CTA 做一个整合收购（roll up），我有数十亿美元去买下他们的业务，我四处奔走——因为我认识他们——给他们打电话、开出报价，绝大多数都接受了，那么如今我就拥有了这 2500 亿美元容量中的 2000 亿。

turns.en: I bought them all and I specifically did so with no consolidation,
turns.zh: 我把他们全买了下来，而且我特意是在不做任何整合的情况下这么做的，

turns.en: no operational nothing. I said, please do what you're doing, you're good at it.
turns.zh: 不做运营整合，什么都不做。我说：请继续做你们正在做的事，你们擅长这个。

turns.en: I'd be a single Trend follower with $200 billion under management and my performance would be exactly the same than if I didn't.
turns.zh: 我会成为一个管理着 2000 亿美元的单一趋势跟踪者，而我的业绩会跟我没这么做时一模一样。

turns.en: This whole narrative that a trend follower can get too big and somehow the returns will go away.
turns.zh: 那种“趋势跟踪者会变得太大、回报不知怎么就消失了”的整套叙事——

turns.en: No, not if they compensate for it by same thought experiment. What if you just diversify the number of approaches you have now? It wouldn't be a criticism, might even be a compliment for someone to say, but if you did that, you would no longer have an edge to the industry, you would be the industry and they would be right in this particular case.
turns.zh: 不，不成立，只要他们对此做了相应的补偿。用同一个思想实验：如果你现在只是把自己所用方法的数量做了分散化呢？那就不算批评，甚至可能是一句恭维——但如果你真那么做了，你就不再是相对行业拥有优势了，你就是这个行业本身，在这种特定情形下他们就说对了。

turns.en: But that kind of gets back to. That's another way to replicate if you will. You don't just have to follow. You could end up running hundreds of different kinds of systematic approaches and at some point you will become average.
turns.zh: 但这又多少回到了——如果你愿意这么说，那是另一种“复制”。你不一定非得去跟踪，你最后可能运行着数百种不同的系统化方法，而到了某个点，你就会变得平庸（average）。

turns.en: Maybe as a little follow up question on that, if we then go to a company specific situation and I think this is where, and you may not agree with this, but I seem to feel that over the last three or four decades, from time to time we've seen companies that probably overstepped their capacity.
turns.zh: 也许就此再问一个小小的后续问题：如果我们转到某家公司的具体情况——我想正是在这里，也许你未必同意，但我似乎感觉到，在过去三四十年来，我们时不时会看到一些公司大概超出了自己的容量。

turns.en: And I was wondering from your perspective, how do you know as a manager that you've reached capacity in. And again, let's just keep it simple, let's just stay with trend that. You know, most people on this listen to the show, they know what, what it is.
turns.zh: 我就想从你的角度问问：作为一名管理人，你怎么知道自己已经达到了容量上限？我们还是把它简单化，就停留在趋势上——你知道，听这档节目的大多数人，他们都清楚那是什么。

turns.en: How, how do we as trend followers really know when it's time to stop trading more assets.
turns.zh: 那么，作为趋势跟踪者，我们究竟怎么知道该在什么时候停止交易更多资产？

turns.en: Well, I think first of all, your premise is demonstrably true. There are managers that have overstepped their capacity less so I think in long term trend following than in other categories we could talk about that are more sensitive to capacity.
turns.zh: 嗯，我想首先，你的前提是明确成立的。确实有管理人超出了自己的容量——我认为在长期趋势跟踪里这种情况较少，而在其他一些我们可以谈到的、对容量更敏感的类别里则更多。

turns.en: So real problem confounding that problem is that reflexivity we talked about between manager and client. If a, if a manager wanted to add or diversify their methodologies to accommodate more size and to have less of a footprint in the market, they would be fighting the impression of style drift or of changing what they're doing in front of their clients.
turns.zh: 而真正让这个问题变得复杂的，是我们谈到的那种管理人与客户之间的反身性。如果一名管理人想增加或分散自己的方法论，以容纳更大的规模、并在市场上留下更少的足迹，他们就要去对抗那种“风格漂移”（style drift）的印象，或者说在客户面前改变自己做法的印象。

turns.en: So that would require a very trusting dialogue, probably one that can't occur fast enough if they're raising assets too fast, because those kinds of changes practically need to take place over years for client acceptance.
turns.zh: 所以那需要一场非常基于信任的对话，而如果他们募资太快，这样的对话很可能来不及发生，因为这类改变实际上需要历经数年才能被客户所接受。

turns.en: Not if you have a good run of asset raising. But I think the real question is how do you tell? And I think everyone who's a listener pretty much understands that liquidity in the marketplace is the key question for any given market.
turns.zh: 如果你有一段时间募资很顺，那就未必。但我认为真正的问题是：你怎么判断？我想每一位听众都大致明白，市场中的流动性（liquidity）是任何一个特定市场的关键问题。

turns.en: And liquidity is dynamic. It's not consistently present, depends on time of day market.
turns.zh: 而流动性是动态的。它并非始终存在，取决于一天中的时段、取决于市场。

turns.en: And it really gets back again to there's a participant on the other side of each trade.
turns.zh: 这真的又回到了那点：每一笔交易的对家都有一个参与者。

turns.en: In the generic terms, a large volume of dollars trying to go into a smaller market more rapidly is going to press a market and cause a capacity issue in this case, if we use that term, but just going to simply move the market, you're going to have slippage, very small amount of money in a large market slowly, and it won't.
turns.zh: 用一般化的说法，一大笔资金试图更快地进入一个较小的市场，就会对这个市场形成压力、造成容量问题——如果我们用那个词的话——而只是单纯地推动市场，你就会产生滑点（slippage）。而一小笔资金缓慢地进入一个大市场，就不会。

turns.en: And so I think if people are very diligent about seeing the fingerprint of their execution costs and their execution alpha and they begin to see their execution costs rise, objectively measured and trend in a particular upward direction, they may have a capacity problem.
turns.zh: 所以我认为，如果人们非常勤勉地去观察自己执行成本（execution costs）和执行阿尔法（execution alpha）的“指纹”，并开始看到自己的执行成本在客观衡量下上升、并朝着某个特定的上行方向形成趋势，那他们可能就存在容量问题。

turns.en: And it very likely could occur. It very likely could be noticed in a few markets long before it's noticed in all markets. It might be noticed in a few markets and then there are questions of whether that's short term or whether that will, you know, that's just a phenomena that the particular country or the particular currency is less liquid and six months later it will return to its liquidity, or it could be because there's just too much money
turns.zh: 它很可能会发生，而且很可能在少数几个市场里被注意到，远早于在所有市场里被注意到。它可能在几个市场里被注意到，然后就有一些问题：那是短期的，还是——你知道——那只是一种现象，即某个特定国家或某种特定货币流动性较差，六个月后它又会恢复到原有的流动性；又或者可能是因为有太多资金

turns.en: there and it's, you know, and it's too tough. If you're a metals trader, you know, you could trade that much in copper, but you can't trade that much in tin. And you're going to have to Decide how to accommodate for that.
turns.zh: 堆在那里，那就太难了。如果你是个金属交易员，你知道，你在铜上可以交易那么多量，但在锡上就交易不了那么多。你就得决定如何去应对这一点。

turns.en: Sure. Alan, I know you have a heart cut off today. We've had a few technical issues along the way. So I'm going to give you the rest of our conversation. And you asked the last few questions that you want.
turns.zh: 好的。Alan，我知道你今天有一个硬性截止时间（hard cut-off）。我们一路上遇到了几个技术问题。所以我要把我们对话剩下的时间交给你，你来问你想问的最后几个问题。

turns.en: You and I could talk anytime if you want. That's good. I think we will have to do a follow up anyways, that's for sure.
turns.zh: 你和我随时都可以聊，如果你想的话。那很好。我想不管怎样我们都得做一次后续访谈，那是肯定的。

turns.en: Just one theme. I mean we have talked about this, we've talked about regime change, we've talked about new market participants, pod shops, microstructure changing from a macro perspective. Markets have changed since you started trading.
turns.zh: 就一个主题。我的意思是，我们已经谈过这个，我们谈过市场状态变化（regime change），谈过新的市场参与者、pod shop、微观结构从宏观角度的变化。自从你开始交易以来，市场已经变了。

turns.en: 2010S were very different, 2000s. Now we're into a new regime.
turns.zh: 2010 年代与 2000 年代非常不同。如今我们进入了一个新的市场状态（regime）。

turns.en: So I guess the question is do you just try and design systems that are robust regardless of how microstructure and macro factors might change over time or do you take that into account and try and incorporate that into your research process?
turns.zh: 所以我想问题是：你是仅仅去设计那种无论微观结构和宏观因素随时间如何变化都保持稳健（robust）的系统，还是你会把这些因素考虑进去、并试图将它们纳入你的研究过程？

turns.en: What do you see as a more kind of effective, robust way of having a research process? I guess the answers I think are all yes.
turns.zh: 在你看来，什么是一种更有效、更稳健的研究过程方式？我想答案大概是“都是肯定的”。

turns.en: I don't think you can avoid not looking in practice. If we were thinking of a trend following sleeve and there's a big question, why would you even want different strategies, for instance? But let's just say you do.
turns.zh: 我认为在实践中你没法回避不去看这些。如果我们在设想一个趋势跟踪的分支（sleeve），这里有个大问题：比如说，你为什么会想要不同的策略？但我们姑且假设你要。

turns.en: If you look at a trend following sleeve and if holding periods are relatively long and execution is extremely insensitive, meaning like for your listeners, if you had a, a trading approach that you could trade the next day or the next day and it would have the same results, you have one that's relatively insensitive to market timing.
turns.zh: 如果你看一个趋势跟踪分支，如果持有期相对较长、执行极度不敏感——意思是，对你们的听众来说，如果你有一种交易方法，你今天交易还是明天交易结果都一样，那你这个方法对市场择时就相对不敏感。

turns.en: If you have one that if you delay by 15 minutes you lose 20% of your P and L, you have one that's pretty time sensitive and the ones that are more time sensitive and the ones that are, you know, their impact and microstructure obviously are a bigger research topic and a bigger capacity concern.
turns.zh: 如果你有一种方法，你只要延迟 15 分钟就会损失 20% 的盈亏（P&L），那你就有了一个相当时间敏感的方法。而那些更时间敏感的、你知道、它们在微观结构上的影响显然是一个更大的研究课题，也是一个更大的容量隐忧。

turns.en: To your earlier question and frankly have I think less margin of error in forward application. You have to be humble enough to, you know, recognize, you know, which is sort of the key aspect I think of all trading is objectivity and objectivity.
turns.zh: 就你前面的问题而言，坦白说，这些方法在向前应用时的容错余地（margin of error）更小。你必须足够谦逊地去认识到——你知道，这算是我认为所有交易的关键方面——那就是客观性（objectivity），客观性。

turns.en: The mana, the emotional manifestation of that is humility. You have to be looking and then that fuels research.
turns.zh: 而它的那种……它在情绪上的体现就是谦逊（humility）。你必须一直在观察，而这就会为研究提供动力。

turns.en: I don't know that that the way I usually think of regime is, it's more a bias because I'm used to that term. More from the macro perspective are rates rising, rates falling, inflation up, inflation down.
turns.zh: 我不确定——我通常思考市场状态的方式，更多是一种偏向，因为我习惯了那个词，更多是从宏观角度：利率在升、利率在降、通胀上行、通胀下行。

turns.en: I think investors are both benefit from those regime considerations, but I think they also are One of the things that ends up fooling
turns.zh: 我认为投资者既会从这些市场状态的考量中受益，但我认为它们也是最终会愚弄

turns.en: early investors, especially early quants. I think the first stage of somebody who comes to the market is somebody who thinks that when data changes in the market that somehow the market moves.
turns.zh: 早期投资者、尤其是早期量化人（quants）的东西之一。我认为一个刚进入市场的人的第一个阶段，是这样一种人：他认为当市场里的数据发生变化时，市场就会以某种方式随之波动。

turns.en: And they constantly trying to model this sort of two body problem
turns.zh: 于是他们不断地试图去建模这个类似“两体问题”（two body problem）的东西，

turns.en: and then they do all kinds of sensitivity analysis and they can't figure out why sometimes this amount of unemployment report change had this big of a market move and other times they don't.
turns.zh: 然后他们做各种各样的敏感性分析，却怎么也想不明白：为什么有时候这么大幅度的失业率报告变化会带来这么大的市场波动，而另一些时候却不会。

turns.en: And relatively rapidly one realizes there aren't two bodies in the market, the data doesn't.
turns.zh: 于是相对很快地，一个人就意识到：市场里并不存在两个“体”，数据本身并不会（买卖）。

turns.en: And data changes and surprises don't buy or sell anything. People see those signals, people see those surprises, people see those changes and then people buy.
turns.zh: 数据的变化和意外本身并不会买入或卖出任何东西。是人看到那些信号、人看到那些意外、人看到那些变化，然后人才去买卖。

turns.en: And there are entire regimes where some data is simply important and then later on it's ignored because it's felt to be.
turns.zh: 而且有些完整的市场状态里，某些数据就是很重要，然后到后来它又被忽略，因为人们觉得它……

turns.en: When I first started trading, the M1, M2 and M3 money supply used to be on the front page of the Wall Street Journal. And because everybody followed money Supply, I think if I hired a new young person today and they hadn't necessarily had specific training in macroeconomics specifically, but were brilliant, they would never even, it would, the topic would never even occur to them unless it was brought up.
turns.zh: 当我刚开始做交易时，M1、M2、M3 货币供应量（money supply）过去常常登在 Wall Street Journal 的头版。因为人人都关注货币供应量——我想如果我今天雇一个新人，一个年轻人，他未必专门受过宏观经济学训练，但很聪明，那么这个话题他甚至根本就不会想到，除非有人提起来。

turns.en: Because today it's muted. Right. And so regimes are also what information is important, I think to the trading community and the investing community at the time. And that fluxes over time.
turns.zh: 因为今天它已经被淡化了。对。所以市场状态也是指：在当时，对交易圈和投资圈而言，什么信息是重要的。而这会随时间不断流动变化。

turns.en: I think it's always will be an imperfect process. And I know you've done some, I think great work in regime shifting and I know I've read your opinion. It is an imperfect process.
turns.zh: 我认为这永远都会是一个不完美的过程。我知道你在市场状态切换（regime shifting）方面做过一些我认为很出色的工作，我也知道我读过你的观点。它就是一个不完美的过程。

turns.en: It's a shift. It's not a precise prediction, but it falls into that category. What I said earlier is the setup, you know, markets. You might want to trade differently in a high inflation, rising interest rate, supply constrained world than you might want to do in a demand constrained, low interest rate, low inflation world.
turns.zh: 它是一种切换，不是一个精确的预测，但它属于那个范畴。我前面说的是入场设置，你知道，市场。在一个高通胀、利率上升、供给受限的世界里，你想交易的方式，可能与你在一个需求受限、低利率、低通胀的世界里想交易的方式不同。

turns.en: And in fact I would even assert that you should. But other people will find their own answer and then they'll have to get convicted by it. And if they stay with it, steady handedness.
turns.zh: 事实上我甚至会断言你就应该这么做。但其他人会找到他们自己的答案，然后他们必须对它产生坚定的信念。而如果他们坚持它——手要稳（steady handedness）。

turns.en: Somebody asked me what's the biggest input to compounding and once I said, well, it's actually how much your hand shakes. Steady handedness compounds well the return gap, the negative investor alpha that occurs from people switching on performance
turns.zh: 有人问过我，复利（compounding）最大的输入是什么，有一次我说：嗯，其实是你手抖得有多厉害。手稳能让复利很好地累积。而那种回报差距——那种由人们根据业绩来回切换而产生的、负的投资者阿尔法（investor alpha）——

turns.en: is usually the biggest cost that they face in putting their portfolios together.
turns.zh: 通常是他们在构建自己组合时面临的最大成本。

turns.en: Probably a good, a good way to end our conversation today. I feel there's definitely enough to talk about in a follow up conversation. Pat, this was really wonderful, you know We've done a lot of these conversations and I think today again we learned something new.
turns.zh: 这大概是为我们今天的对话收尾的一个很好的方式。我觉得肯定还有足够多的内容可以留到后续访谈里再谈。Pat，这次真的太精彩了，你知道，我们做过很多这样的对话，而我认为今天我们又一次学到了新东西。

turns.en: You spoke about things even though it's a well known topic but in a different way and it really benefits everyone listening. So I really, really appreciate your time and your insights.
turns.zh: 你谈到的一些东西，尽管是个众所周知的话题，但你用了一种不同的方式来讲，这真的让每一位听众都受益匪浅。所以我真的、真的非常感谢你的时间和你的洞见。

turns.en: And as I said, I hope we will be doing this again in the not too distant future.
turns.zh: 正如我说的，我希望在不久的将来我们还能再做一次。

turns.en: And to all of you listening today, I hope you were also able to take something away from today's conversation onto your own investment journey. And if you did, please share this episode along with the others with your friends and colleagues from Pat, Alan and me.

Look forward to being back with you as we continue our conversations on Top Traders Unplugged and we we continue deep dive into the CTA industry and in the meantime of course check out the show notes for all these episodes where you also find links to Pat's firm and to Alan's resources as well.

turns.zh: 好了，无论如何，照惯例，让我以这句话来收尾：照顾好自己，也照顾好彼此。
